summary: John's 6th-great-grandfather and his only proven Revolutionary patriot (SAR P-232580, DAR A068239): ensign in the Orange County, NY militia who pioneered Plymouth and Jackson Twp, PA.
bio: Thomas Lamoreaux was born about 1745 (SAR supplemental application gives c.1745-1829; tree 1746-1829), of Huguenot descent (Harvey Book p.135: the family descended from Huguenots who left France after the revocation of the Edict of Nantes). His parents were probably Jean (John) Lamoreaux (1723-1809) and Charity Davenport; the SAR approved a 2017 supplemental application tracing patriot John Lamoreaux to Thomas, though the 1919 Lamoureux Record leaves Thomas in either John's or Peter's family. In 1775 he signed the Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct, Orange Co., alongside 'James Tuttle' (probably his wife's brother). In 1776 he was ensign of the Woodbury Clove company ('Thos. Lammoreux, ensign') under Capt. Francis Smith - very probably his wife Keturah's uncle - in the regiment of Colonel Woodhull, very probably Col. Jesse Woodhull, a cousin of Keturah. He is SAR Patriot P-232580 and DAR ancestor A068239. He married Keturah Tuttle. In spring 1790 he moved to Plymouth, Luzerne Co., and by October 1790 served in Capt. George P. Ransom's militia company (Harvey Book p.355) - so the family was not in the valley for the 1778 Wyoming Massacre. With Thomas Case he headed the pioneers who 'scaled the northern wall of the valley, the Shawnee mountain' before 1800, settling in Jackson Twp; 'the vast extent and character of the stone wall upon the farms of these two old settlers were a matter of marvel in early days... the miles of it to-day... are a monument of the toil', and one of his six sons was pointed out 'for having laid so many feet of stone wall in a day' (Wright pp.399-400). His will (15 Apr 1815, codicil 9 Nov 1826, registered 5 Oct 1829, Luzerne Will Book A pp.341-3) disinherited son James 'on account of his disobedience to me', gave James's crippled son Jewel ('Jewel Lamoreaux a cripple child') a share equal with his daughters, cut son John's bequest to $50 'considering... the privileges already he has had', cut Thomas Jr. out for 'interference and bad conduct' (his share to grandson Wesley), and left wife Keturah his 'best horse saddle & bridle' and $100. Burial: the SAR record says Shupp's Cemetery, Larksville; the family burying ground is on the Lamoreaux farm at Chase, Jackson Twp (Tilling Point Farm), where a DAR marker was placed in 2017. His Find a Grave grave marker calls him a War of 1812 private - he would have been about 67, so this is possibly his son. WikiTree's tradition that he was held on a Long Island prison ship is unverified. All three approved SAR applications (1995, 2014, 2017) descend through his sons James or Thomas, none through Martha.
